title: Your day-one note before you type
heading: Before you type a word
caption: Four lines to a brand-new colleague. Thirty seconds. Then type.

context.title: Context
context.question: What would you tell them about your situation?
context.caption: Budget, headcount, culture, what happened last year.

tools.title: Tools
tools.question: What would they need access to?
tools.caption: The booking system, the caterers you trust, the calendar.

brief.title: Brief
brief.question: What exactly are you asking for?
brief.caption: One structured plan, due by end of day.

check.title: Check
check.question: How will you review their work?
check.caption: Read it as your team lead will, before it leaves your desk.

write-it-down.header: Write it down, or it is gone
write-it-down.description: Instructions given only in chat do not reliably survive compaction; Anthropic advises putting persistent rules in a file the agent reads at the start.[1]

claude-code-memory.title: Anthropic, How Claude remembers your project (Claude Code memory)

short-beats-long.description: Chroma tested 18 models and found performance grows increasingly unreliable as input length grows, even on simple tasks.[1]

context-rot.title: Hong, Troynikov, Huber, Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance

the-habit.title: The habit
the-habit.keywords: the habit, before you type a word, thirty seconds, brand-new colleague on day one
the-habit.script: So here is the habit, and it is small. Next time you reach for AI on something real, before you type a word, stop. Take thirty seconds. Jot down what you would tell a brand-new colleague on day one.

four-lines.title: Four lines
four-lines.keywords: four lines, context, tools, brief, check their work, then type
four-lines.script: Four lines are enough. The context, meaning what they need to know about your situation. The tools they would need. The brief, meaning what exactly you are asking for. And how you will check their work. Then type.
